_comment_about_this_file: Firefox managed-storage values for the Locke extension.
Drop into the path matching your platform - see the comment in
firefox-policies.json for the full path list. The file MUST be
named after the gecko id: desktop-connector@sonomos.ai.json
The gecko id still says `desktop-connector` because it is the id
already registered for this add-on (manifest.json,
browser_specific_settings.gecko.id). Changing it would orphan every
existing install, so the old product name survives in the id and
nowhere else.
Firefox reads this file once at startup; restart the browser after
editing. Values land in browser.storage.managed and override the
user's local settings.
The `data` block below maps 1:1 onto managed-schema.json at the repo
root, which is authoritative for every key, type and bound. Only the
names in shared/constants.js::MANAGED_KEYS are read; anything else is
ignored on arrival.
Enforced today: allowedProviders (which catalog providers the shim
screens), heartbeatSeconds (health-probe cadence, 10-600s),
debugLogging (healthy-path console lines only - a blocked or
unscreened send is warned about regardless) and enforceTimeoutMs (how
long a HELD request waits for a verdict before it is BLOCKED,
Accepted and then ignored, so deliberately absent from this template
[documented 2026-09-01]: telemetryEnabled (nothing consults it) and
lockedSettings (there is no popup settings UI, so there is nothing
for it to lock). Setting either changes no behaviour.
allowedProviders takes CATALOG PROVIDER IDS from
shared/ai-surfaces.json - not product nicknames, not API endpoint
names. The accepted values are the enum in managed-schema.json;
tests/shim.test.js pins that enum against the catalog. `[]` or unset
means EVERY catalog surface is screened, which is the default and the
recommended setting. A non-empty list is SUBTRACTIVE - it can only
remove surfaces from screening - and a provider left off it is not
screened at all, so prompts to it leave the machine unexamined.
